_doc: #642 THE ONE DECLARATION of the Store's read-only feeds: the repo's COMMITS and its CI-CD runs. Read by FeedViewer; nothing in Kotlin names a repository, an endpoint, a JSON field or a status word. One tab per entry, in this order, so a third feed (releases, issues, a second repo) is an entry here and no Kotlin at all. FeedViewer is a READER: every row's action is 'open the link the feed itself gave us', so there is nothing here that can install, write or authenticate. That is why these endpoints are the unauthenticated public ones - a token would buy nothing a reader needs and would be one more secret on the device.
_doc_transport: #668 THESE URLS ARE THE ANONYMOUS GITHUB API, AND THAT IS THE KNOWN DEFECT. Anonymous api.github.com is capped at 60 requests/hour PER IP, and an exhausted quota answers 403 with 'API rate limit exceeded for <ip>' - which is the 403 reported on both feeds. Measured 2026-09-30: the same endpoint returned 200 with x-ratelimit-limit 60 / remaining 55, so this is quota exhaustion that self-heals when the window rolls, NOT a permissions problem and NOT a bug in the reader. Note the quota is per IP and the phone shares it with everything else on that address, so unrelated tooling on the same network can spend the Store's budget. THE FIX IS THE TRANSPORT: route these through the fleet's git-proxy-api (#647), which holds the fleet's own GitHub credential server-side so the phone holds none, and authenticate machine-to-machine with Authorization: Bearer (NOT the browser session path, which #655 breaks by dropping the /git prefix on the Authelia return). THAT PROXY CANNOT SERVE THESE TWO FEEDS YET: it exposes exactly /git/health, /git/endpoints, /git/repos and /git/repos/:owner/:repo/tarball, and its router refuses to start unless served routes equal declared ones, so commits and actions/runs must first be added to runtime.endpoints plus handlers in the cloud-u-containers repo. Until they exist, repointing these urls would turn a self-healing 403 into a permanent 404. When they do exist, adopting them is ONLY an edit to the two `url` values here - no Kotlin - and #662 means the proxy is sheddable, so the feed must keep failing out loud. DO NOT add a cache to soften the 403: a stale feed presented as live is worse than a feed that says it could not read.
_doc_fields: `url` is fetched through SourceResolver.getBody, the store's one request path. `per_page` is part of the declared url, so the page size is a data edit like everything else (raised 30 -> 50 for #668). `items` names the array inside the response; omit it when the response IS the array (GitHub's /commits). `title`/`subtitle`/`ref`/`link` are templates: every {a.b.c} is looked up as a dotted path in the item and substituted, and a path the item does not carry substitutes empty - so a feed that changes shape degrades to a thinner row instead of crashing the tab. `ref` is the short identifier drawn at the head of the row (a sha, a run number). `state` is the field whose value is matched against `ok`/`bad` below to colour the row; a value in neither list is drawn neutral, which is what an in-flight run must look like - 'not finished' is not 'failed'.
